translations.idiomatic: cook according to your belly's measure—in wealthy homes, meals left over.

sentences.zh: 非粒實息耗，意有盈虛爾。

translations.literal: It is not that grain truly stops depletion; mind has surplus and deficit.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that grain itself ends want; the mind has its fullness and its lack.

sentences.zh: 況心得優劣，身獲仁富，明白入素，氣志如神，雖十旬九飯，不能令饑，業席三屬，不能為寒。

translations.literal: How much more when the mind gains superiority and inferiority, the body receives benevolence and wealth, clarity enters plainness, breath and will are like spirit—though ten decadads and nine meals, hunger cannot be made; though mat work thrice patched, cold cannot be made.
translations.idiomatic: How much more when the mind knows rank yet the body receives benevolence and plenty, clarity dwells in simplicity, and spirit and will are like the divine: though you eat only nine meals in a hundred days, hunger cannot touch you; though your mat is patched thrice over, cold cannot reach you.

sentences.zh: 豈不信然。

translations.literal: Is this not credible indeed?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not wholly credible?

sentences.zh: :且以己為度者，無以自通彼量。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who measure by self cannot by themselves penetrate others' measure.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who judge by their own measure cannot by themselves grasp another's.

sentences.zh: 渾四游而斡五緯，天道弘也。

translations.literal: Harmonizing the four wanderings and turning the five celestial markers—Heaven's Way is vast.
translations.idiomatic: To embrace the four quarters and turn the five luminaries—that is how vast Heaven's Way is.

sentences.zh: 振河海而載山川，地道厚也。

translations.literal: Shaking rivers and seas and bearing mountains and streams—Earth's Way is thick.
translations.idiomatic: To shake rivers and seas and bear mountains and streams—that is how deep Earth's Way is.

sentences.zh: 一情紀而合流貫，人靈茂也。

translations.literal: One sentiment bound and penetrating flowing currents—human spirit is luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: To bind feeling in one thread and join all flowing currents—that is how rich the human spirit is.

sentences.zh: 昔之通乎此數者，不為剖判之行，必廣其風度，無挾私殊，博其交道，靡懷曲異。

translations.literal: Those of old who mastered these several did not practice conduct of splitting judgment; they must broaden their wind and manner, hold no private difference, widen their way of interchange, harbor no crooked exception.
translations.idiomatic: Those of old who mastered these several truths did not act by splitting and judging; they broadened their bearing, held no private bias, widened their friendships, and harbored no crooked exception.

sentences.zh: 故望塵請友，則義士輕身，一遇拜親，則仁人投分。

translations.literal: Therefore gazing at dust to request friendship, then righteous men lightly risk body; one meeting to bow as kin, then benevolent men cast their share.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the righteous man would lightly risk his life at a glimpse of dust raised by a friend approaching; the benevolent man would pledge his heart at a single meeting sworn as kin.

sentences.zh: 此倫序通允，禮俗平一，上獲其用，下得其和。

translations.literal: This order of human relations is thorough and fair, ritual and custom level and one; above obtains its use, below obtains harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Such was human order made open and fair, ritual and custom leveled as one; above gained what it needed, below found harmony.

sentences.zh: :世務雖移，前休未遠，人之適主，吾將反本。

translations.literal: Though worldly affairs shift, former excellence is not far; men's suiting their lord—I will return to the root.
translations.idiomatic: Though worldly affairs change, the excellence of old is not far off; as men suit themselves to their times, I will return to the root.

sentences.zh: 夫人之生，暫有心識，幼壯驟過，衰耗騖及。

translations.literal: Man's birth briefly has mind and knowing; youth and strength flash past, decay and waste rush upon one.
translations.idiomatic: Human life briefly possesses mind and awareness; youth and vigor flash past, decay and decline rush upon us.

sentences.zh: 其間夭鬱，既難勝言，假獲存遂，又云無幾。

translations.literal: The premature and stifled between—already hard to speak fully; even if one obtains survival and completion, again it is said not many.
translations.idiomatic: The early deaths and stifled lives between are beyond full telling; even if one attains survival and fulfillment, the span is still said to be brief.

sentences.zh: 柔麗之身，亟委土木，剛清之才，遽為丘壤，回遑顧慕，雖數紀之中爾。

translations.literal: Soft lovely bodies quickly entrusted to earth and wood; firm clear talents suddenly become mounds and soil; turning and looking back in longing—even within several decades.
translations.idiomatic: Soft, lovely bodies are soon given to earth and timber; firm, clear talents suddenly become mounds of soil. To turn and look back in longing—even that lasts only a few decades.

sentences.zh: 以此持榮，曾不可留，以此服道，亦何能平。

translations.literal: With this to hold glory, glory could never stay; with this to serve the Way, how could one be at peace?
translations.idiomatic: With this span to cling to glory, glory could never endure; with this span to serve the Way, how could one be at peace?

sentences.zh: 進退我生，遊觀所達，得貴為人，將在含理。

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating in my life, roaming and viewing what is reached—to gain nobility as a person lies in embracing principle.
translations.idiomatic: As I advance and retreat through life and roam where I may, the nobility of being human lies in embracing principle.

sentences.zh: 含理之貴，惟神與交，幸有心靈，義無自惡，偶信天德，逝不上慚。

translations.literal: The nobility of embracing principle is only communing with spirit; fortunate to have mind and soul, in righteousness none self-abasing; by chance trusting Heaven's virtue, in departing not ashamed above.
translations.idiomatic: The worth of embracing principle is communion with spirit alone. Fortunate to have mind and soul, in righteousness I will not demean myself; trusting Heaven's virtue by chance, in death I will not be ashamed before it.

sentences.zh: 欲使人沈來化，志符往哲，勿謂是賒，日鑿斯密。

translations.literal: I wish to make people sink into coming transformation, aspirations matching former sages; do not say this is distant—the day chisels grow close.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to sink others into the transforming force of what is to come and align their wills with the sages of old. Do not call this remote—each day's carving draws it nearer.

sentences.zh: 著通此意，吾將忘老，如曰不然，其誰與歸。

translations.literal: If I make this meaning penetrate, I will forget old age; if you say it is not so, with whom shall I return?
translations.idiomatic: If I can make this meaning penetrate, I shall forget my years; if you say it is not so, with whom shall I go home?

sentences.zh: 偶懷所撰，略布眾條；

translations.literal: As chance moves what I have drafted, I briefly spread the many clauses;
translations.idiomatic: As my thoughts chance upon what I have drafted, I briefly set out these many topics;

sentences.zh: 若備舉情見，顧未書一。

translations.literal: If fully to present feeling and appearance, in a glance not one is written.
translations.idiomatic: if I were to set forth every feeling and circumstance in full, I could not write one clause in a single glance.

sentences.zh: 贍身之經，別在田家節政；

translations.literal: Canon for supporting the body is separately in Farmstead Section on Governance;
translations.idiomatic: The canon for sustaining the body is set out separately in Farmstead Regulations on Governance;

sentences.zh: 奉終之紀，自著燕居畢義。

translations.literal: regulations for observing the end are self-authored in Dwelling at Rest and Completed Rites.
translations.idiomatic: the regulations for observing the end I have written myself in Dwelling at Rest and Rites Completed.

sentences.zh: 劉湛誅，起延之為始興王濬後軍諮議參軍，御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhan was executed, Yanzhi was appointed Consultant of the Rear Army to the Prince of Shixing, Jun, and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zhan was executed, Yanzhi was appointed Consultant of the Rear Army to Prince Shixing Liu Jun and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 在任縱容，無所舉奏。

translations.literal: In office he was indulgent and submitted nothing for impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was lax and brought no impeachments.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、司徒左長史，坐啟買人田，不肯還直，尚書左丞荀赤松奏之曰：「求田問舍，前賢所鄙。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the National University and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education; for memorializing to buy someone's field and refusing to return payment, Left Assistant of the Department of State Affairs Xun Chisong memorialized saying: "Seeking fields and houses—former worthies despised this.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the National University and Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education. For memorializing to buy another man's field and refusing to pay the price, Left Assistant Xun Chisong of the Department of State Affairs memorialized: "To seek fields and houses was despised by the worthies of old.

sentences.zh: 延之唯利是視，輕冒陳聞，依傍詔恩，拒捍餘直，垂及周年，猶不畢了，昧利苟得，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Yanzhi looks only to profit, rashly ventured memorial, leaning on edict grace, resisting the remaining payment—nearly a full year and still not concluded; blinded by profit and grasping gain, without regard for anything.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi looks only to profit, rashly petitioned the throne, leaned on imperial grace, and resisted paying the balance. Nearly a year has passed and the matter is still unsettled. Blinded by gain, he grasps without scruple.

sentences.zh: 延之昔坐事屏斥，復蒙抽進，而曾不悛革，怨誹無已。

translations.literal: Yanzhi once for an affair was expelled and screened, again received selection and advancement, yet never reformed, resentment and slander without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi was once dismissed for an offense, then favored again with promotion, yet he never reformed and his resentment and slander never ceased.

sentences.zh: 交遊闒茸，沈迷麴糵，橫興譏謗，詆毀朝士。

translations.literal: Companions were vulgar rabble, sunk in yeasts and brews, recklessly raising ridicule, calumniating court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: His companions were vulgar rabble; he wallowed in wine and brew, recklessly spread ridicule, and slandered court officials.

sentences.zh: 仰竊過榮，增憤薄之性；

translations.literal: Looking up he stole excess glory, increasing irascible shallow nature;
translations.idiomatic: Looking up he stole more honor than was his due, feeding his irascible and shallow temper;

sentences.zh: 私恃顧盻，成強梁之心。

translations.literal: privately relying on turning glances, forming a bully's heart.
translations.idiomatic: privately relying on imperial favor, he formed the heart of a bully.

sentences.zh: 外示寡求，內懷奔競，干祿祈遷，不知極已，預讌班觴，肆罵上席。

translations.literal: Outwardly showing few desires, inwardly harboring race for advancement, seeking salary and praying for promotion, not knowing limit for self; at preliminary feast with class cups, wantonly cursing the upper seats.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he showed few desires; inwardly he raced for advancement, sought salary and prayed for promotion, and knew no limit. At banquets by rank he wantonly reviled his superiors.

sentences.zh: 山海含容，每存遵養，愛兼彫蟲，未忍遐棄，而驕放不節，日月彌著。

translations.literal: Mountains and seas contain and tolerate, always preserving followed nurture; love extending even to carved insects, not bearing to cast far away—but pride and license without restraint grow day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Like mountains and seas the throne contains and tolerates, always nurturing those it keeps; it loves even the smallest talent and is loath to cast them off—yet his pride and license grow more flagrant day by day.

sentences.zh: 臣聞聲問過情，孟軻所恥，況聲非外來，問由己出，雖心智薄劣，而高自比擬，客氣虛張，曾無愧畏，豈可復弼亮五教，增曜台階。

translations.literal: Your servant hears: reputation and inquiry exceeding truth—Mencius was ashamed of this; how much more when reputation is not from outside but inquiry from oneself issuing! Though mind and wisdom are thin and inferior, yet he highly compares himself; guest air vainly inflated, never having shame and fear—how could he again assist and brighten the five teachings, add luster to the terrace steps?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that reputation exceeding the truth was what Mencius despised—how much more when the reputation is not given from outside but sought by oneself! Though his mind and talent are slight, he compares himself to the great; his manner is inflated with false pride and he knows no shame. How can he again assist and illumine the five teachings and add luster to the terrace steps?

sentences.zh: 請以延之訟田不實，妄干天聽，以強凌弱，免所居官。」

translations.literal: I request that for Yanzhi's lawsuit over fields being untrue, rashly disturbing Heaven's hearing, using strength to bully weakness, he be removed from the office he holds."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Yanzhi be removed from his office for his false suit over the field, his rash disturbance of Heaven's hearing, and his use of power to bully the weak."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 復為祕書監，光祿勳，太常。

translations.literal: He was again Director of the Secretariat, Superintendent of Guanglu, and Grand Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Director of the Secretariat, Superintendent of Guanglu, and Grand Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時沙門釋慧琳，以才學為太祖所賞愛，每召見，常升獨榻，延之甚疾焉。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Shì Huilin, for talent and learning was enjoyed and favored by the Founding Emperor—whenever summoned he often rose to a solitary couch—Yanzhi greatly detested this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Huilin, prized by Emperor Wen for his talent and learning, was often summoned and regularly given a separate couch. Yanzhi detested this deeply.

sentences.zh: 因醉白上曰：「昔同子參乘，袁絲正色。

translations.literal: Drunk he told the Emperor: "In old times when Zisi shared the carriage, Yuan Ang showed stern color.
translations.idiomatic: Once, drunk, he told the emperor: "In old times when the crown prince shared the carriage with others, Yuan Ang kept a stern countenance.

sentences.zh: 此三台之坐，豈可使刑餘居之。」

translations.literal: This seat of the Three Terraces—how can it allow a castrated man to sit there!"
translations.idiomatic: This is the seat of the Three Excellencies—how can a castrated man be allowed to occupy it!"

sentences.zh: 上變色。

translations.literal: The Emperor changed color.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face changed.

sentences.zh: 延之性既褊激，兼有酒過，肆意直言，曾無遏隱，故論者多不知云。

translations.literal: Yanzhi's nature was narrow and volatile, and together with faults of wine he spoke straight from desire without ever restraining or hiding—therefore many who discussed him did not know how to speak of him.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi's nature was narrow and impulsive, and with the fault of wine he spoke bluntly without restraint or concealment; therefore many commentators scarcely knew what to say of him.

sentences.zh: 居身清約，不營財利，布衣蔬食，獨酌郊野，當其為適，傍若無人。

translations.literal: In person he was pure and sparing, not managing wealth and profit; cloth coat and vegetable food, drinking alone in suburbs and fields—when it suited him, those beside seemed not to exist.
translations.idiomatic: In his person he was frugal and pure, sought no wealth, wore plain cloth and ate simple food, and drank alone in the countryside; when he was at ease, those beside him might as well not exist.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，上表自陳曰：「臣聞行百里者半於九十，言其末路之難也。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he submitted a memorial stating his case: "Your servant hears: he who walks a hundred li is halfway at ninety—so the words speak of how hard the final stretch is.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he submitted a memorial stating his case: "Your servant has heard that he who walks a hundred li is only halfway at ninety—that saying speaks of how hard the final stretch is.

sentences.zh: 愚心常謂為虛，方今乃知其信。

translations.literal: This fool's heart always thought it empty; only now do I know it is true.
translations.idiomatic: This fool's heart always took it for empty talk; only now do I know it is true.

sentences.zh: 臣延之人薄寵厚，宿塵國言，而雪効無從，榮牒增廣，曆盡身彫，日叨官次，雖容載有塗，而妨穢滋積。

translations.literal: Your servant Yanzhi—person thin yet favor thick, long dust of state words, yet snow-like effect without follow-through, glory registers ever broader; years exhausted body carved, daily grasping office rank—though the carriage has a road, yet hindrance and filth accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant Yanzhi is slight in person yet thick in favor, long stained by court rumor, yet with no chance to clear his name; his honors ever broaden, his years exhaust his body, and daily he clings to office. Though the carriage still has a road, hindrances and filth only pile higher.

sentences.zh: 早欲啟請餘算，屏蔽醜老。

translations.literal: Long I wished to open request for remaining reckonings, to screen ugliness and old age.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago I wished to petition for what years remain and hide my ugly old age.

sentences.zh: 但時制行及，歸慕無賒，是以腆冒愆非，簡息干黷。

translations.literal: But the times' regulations pressed on conduct and return longing had no margin—therefore I thickly transgressed faults and briefly rested disturbing the throne.
translations.idiomatic: But the times' regulations pressed upon me and longing to return left no delay; therefore I shamelessly transgressed and briefly ceased troubling the throne.

sentences.zh: 耗歇難支，質用有限，自去夏侵暑，入此秋變，頭齒眩疼，根痼漸劇，手足冷痺，左胛尤甚。

translations.literal: Wasted exhaustion hard to support, substance and use limited—from last summer's invasive heat into this autumn's change, head and teeth dizzy with pain, root affliction gradually severe, hands and feet cold and numb, left shoulder blade especially so.
translations.idiomatic: My strength is spent and hard to sustain; my substance and capacity are limited. Since last summer's oppressive heat and into this autumn's change, my head and teeth swim with pain, my chronic ailment grows worse, my hands and feet are cold and numb, and my left shoulder especially.

sentences.zh: 素不能食，頃向減半。

translations.literal: By nature unable to eat; recently my intake halved.
translations.idiomatic: By nature I eat poorly; recently my intake has halved.

sentences.zh: 本猶賴服食，比倦悸遠晚，年疾所催，顧景引日。

translations.literal: Originally I still relied on taking medicine; recently weariness and palpitation came far late, yearly illness pressing on me, turning my head the days are drawn out.
translations.idiomatic: I had still relied on medicines; now weariness and palpitation come early, age and illness press upon me, and when I turn my head the days seem to lengthen.

sentences.zh: 臣班叨首卿，位尸封典，肅祗朝校，尚恧匪任，而陵廟眾事，有以疾怠，宮府覲慰，轉闕躬親。

translations.literal: Your servant's rank usurps chief minister, position a corpse of seals and canon; reverent in court rites and schools, still ashamed of unfit duty—yet mausoleum affairs many, there is slackness from illness; palace offices' viewing condolences, increasingly lacking my person to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's rank usurps the chief minister's place and holds the seals of state in name alone; though reverent toward court rites and schools, I am still ashamed of unfitness for duty. Yet in the many affairs of mausoleum and temple I slacken through illness, and in palace condolences I increasingly fail to attend in person.

sentences.zh: 息㚟庸微，過宰近邑，回澤爰降，實加將監，乞解所職，隨就藥養。

translations.literal: Son Jun is commonplace and slight, passing through near district as magistrate; favor and grace descended, truly adding my being overseen—I beg to resign my offices and follow to drug nurture.
translations.idiomatic: My son Jun is slight in talent and serves as magistrate of a nearby district; imperial favor has descended upon him, which only adds to my being watched—I beg to resign my offices and retire to medical care.

sentences.zh: 伏願聖慈，特垂矜許。

translations.literal: Bowing head I wish sagely compassion, especially to let down pity and permit.
translations.idiomatic: Prostrate, I beg Your Sage compassion especially to grant pity and approval.

sentences.zh: 禀恩明世，負報冥暮，仰企端闈，上戀罔極。」

translations.literal: Receiving grace in bright world, bearing repayment in dim dusk—looking up to the palace gate-end, above longing without limit."
translations.idiomatic: Having received grace in this bright age, I shall repay it in the dark of evening; looking up to the palace gate, my longing for Your Majesty knows no bound."

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: Not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: His request was not granted.

sentences.zh: 明年致事。

translations.literal: The next year he resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he resigned his office.

sentences.zh: 元凶弒立，以為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the usurper prince murdered and established himself, [Yanzhi] was made Grand Master of Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: When the usurper Liu Shao murdered his father and took the throne, Yanzhi was made Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 先是，子竣為世祖南中郎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Before this, his son Jun had been Consulting Colonel of the Southern Staff to Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, his son Yan Jun had been Consulting Colonel on the Southern Staff of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 及義師入討，竣參定密謀，兼造書檄。

translations.literal: When the righteous army entered to punish, Jun joined in fixing secret plans and also drafted the proclamations.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army marched to punish the usurper, Jun took part in the secret plans and also drafted the proclamations.

sentences.zh: 劭召延之，示以檄文，問曰：「此筆誰所造﹖」延之曰：「竣之筆也。」

translations.literal: Shao summoned Yanzhi, showed him the proclamation document, and asked: "Whose brush made this?" Yanzhi said: "Jun's brush."
translations.idiomatic: Shao summoned Yanzhi, showed him the proclamation, and asked, "Whose hand wrote this?" Yanzhi said, "My son Jun's hand."

sentences.zh: 又問：「何以知之﹖」延之曰：「竣筆體，臣不容不識。」

translations.literal: He asked again: "How do you know?" Yanzhi said: "Jun's brush style—your servant could not fail to know."
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "How do you know?" Yanzhi said, "Jun's style of writing—your servant could not fail to know it."

sentences.zh: 劭又曰：「言辭何至乃爾。」

translations.literal: Shao also said: "How could the words reach such a point!"
translations.idiomatic: Shao also said, "How could the language go so far!"

sentences.zh: 延之曰：「竣尚不顧老父，何能為陛下。」

translations.literal: Yanzhi said: "Jun does not even care for his old father—how could he do it for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi said, "Jun does not even care for his aged father—how could he serve Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 劭意乃釋，由是得免。

translations.literal: Shao's intent was then released; because of this he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shao's suspicion was then lifted, and because of this Yanzhi was spared.

sentences.zh: 世祖登阼，以為金紫光祿大夫，領湘東王師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu came to the throne, Yanzhi was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon and concurrently Tutor to the Prince of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 子竣既貴重，權傾一朝，凡所資供，延之一無所受，器服不改，宅宇如舊。

translations.literal: His son Jun had already become noble and weighty, his power tilting the whole court; of all supplies offered, Yanzhi accepted none—his vessels and garments unchanged, his dwelling as before.
translations.idiomatic: When his son Jun rose to power and swayed the court, Yanzhi accepted none of the provisions sent him; his furnishings and dress stayed as they were, his house unchanged.

sentences.zh: 常乘羸牛笨車，逢竣鹵簿，即屏往道側。

translations.literal: He often rode a lean ox in a clumsy cart; when he met Jun's guard of honor, he would withdraw to the roadside.
translations.idiomatic: He often rode a scrawny ox in a plain cart; whenever he met Jun's guard of honor, he would pull aside to the edge of the road.

sentences.zh: 又好騎馬，遨游里巷，遇知舊輒據鞍索酒，得酒必頹然自得。

translations.literal: He also loved riding horses and roaming lanes and alleys; meeting old acquaintances he would lean on the saddle and demand wine, and once he got wine he would always sink into satisfied abandon.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved to ride through the lanes; when he met old friends he would halt in the saddle and demand wine, and once he had it he would sink into contented ease.

sentences.zh: 常語竣曰：「平生不喜見要人，今不幸見汝。」

translations.literal: He often told Jun: "All my life I have disliked meeting important men—now unhappily I meet you."
translations.idiomatic: He often told Jun, "All my life I have hated meeting the powerful—now, unhappily, I meet you."

sentences.zh: 竣起宅，謂曰：「善為之，無令後人笑汝拙也。」

translations.literal: When Jun built a mansion, he said to him: "Build it well—do not let later men laugh at your clumsiness."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun built a mansion, he told him, "Build it well—do not let posterity laugh at your lack of taste."

sentences.zh: 表解師職，加給親信三十人。

translations.literal: He memorialized to resign the tutorship and was given thirty personal attendants in addition.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to resign the tutorship and was granted thirty personal attendants in addition.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，卒，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian (456), he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian (456) he died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 追贈散騎常侍、特進，金紫光祿大夫如故。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Special Advancement, with Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and Special Advancement, while retaining his rank as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.

sentences.zh: 諡曰憲子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xianzi (The Principled).
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous title was Xianzi, "The Principled."

sentences.zh: 延之與陳郡謝靈運俱以詞彩齊名，自潘岳、陸機之後，文士莫及也，江左稱顏、謝焉。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen commandery were both famed for equal brilliance in letters; since Pan Yue and Lu Ji, no man of letters could match them—the Eastern Jin called them Yan and Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and Xie Lingyun of Chen were equally famed for literary brilliance; since Pan Yue and Lu Ji, no writer had matched them—the south spoke of Yan and Xie.

sentences.zh: 所著並傳於世。

translations.literal: All that he wrote has been handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His writings have all been handed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 竣別有傳。

translations.literal: Jun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jun has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 竣弟測，亦以文章見知，官至江夏王義恭大司徒錄事參軍，蚤卒。

translations.literal: Jun's younger brother Ce was also known for his writings; his office reached Recorder and Retainer under the Grand Minister of Works for Prince Yigong of Jiangxia, and he died early.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's younger brother Ce was also known for his writing; he rose to Recorder under Prince Yigong of Jiangxia's Grand Minister of Works and died young.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔曰：「延之昔師訓朕躬，情契兼款。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming acceded, an edict said: "Yanzhi once instructed and admonished Our person; affection and trust were both warm.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming came to the throne, an edict read: "Yanzhi once instructed and admonished Us; Our bond with him was warm and trusting.

sentences.zh: 前記室參軍、濟陽太守㚟伏勤蕃朝，綢繆恩舊。

translations.literal: Former Recorder of the Staff and Administrator of Jiyang Fu served diligently at the princely court, binding close ties of old favor.
translations.idiomatic: Former Recorder of the Staff and Administrator of Jiyang, Fu, served diligently at the princely court and kept close the bonds of old favor.

sentences.zh: 可擢為中書侍郎。」

translations.literal: He may be promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 㚟，延之第三子也。

translations.literal: Fu was Yanzhi's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was Yanzhi's third son.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：出身事主，雖義在忘私，至於君親兩事，既無同濟，為子為臣，各隨其時可也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Leaving one's person to serve a lord—though righteousness lies in forgetting the private self—as for the two affairs of lord and parent, since they cannot be crossed together, to be son and to be minister, each follows what the time allows.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: To leave home and serve a lord asks one to set private feeling aside; yet lord and parent are not duties one can fulfill together—as son and as minister, each must follow what the time permits.

sentences.zh: 若夫馳文道路，軍政恒儀，成敗所因，非繫乎此。

translations.literal: As for dispatching writings on the road and the constant forms of military and civil affairs—the causes of success and failure do not hang on this.
translations.idiomatic: As for dispatching proclamations on campaign and the fixed forms of civil and military rule, success and failure do not depend on that.

sentences.zh: 而據筆數罪，陵讎犯逆，餘彼慈親，垂之虎吻，以此為忠，無聞前誥。

translations.literal: Yet to take up the brush and count crimes, to insult the foe and denounce rebellion, leaving aside that kindly parent and handing him to the tiger's maw—calling this loyalty has no hearing in former admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: Yet to take up the brush and list crimes, to revile the enemy and denounce rebellion, abandoning one's loving father and delivering him to the tiger's maw—to call that loyalty finds no warrant in the admonitions of old.

sentences.zh: 夫自忍其親，必將忍人之親，自忘其孝，期以申人之孝，食子放鹿，斷可識矣。

translations.literal: One who can bear against his own parent will surely bear against others' parents; one who forgets his own filial piety expects to extend others' filial piety—Yi Yin who ate his son and Duke Huan who released the deer: this can clearly be known.
translations.idiomatic: He who can harden himself against his own parent will harden himself against others' parents; he who forgets his own filial duty expects to fulfill others'—as with Yi Yin who ate his son, or Duke Huan who freed the deer, the pattern is plain.

sentences.zh: 記云：「八十者一子不從政，九十者家不從政。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "When a man is eighty, one son does not enter government; when he is ninety, the household does not enter government."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "At eighty, one son is excused from office; at ninety, the whole household is excused."

sentences.zh: 豈不以年薄桑榆，憂患將及，雖有職王朝，許以辭事，況顛沛之道，慮在未測者乎。

translations.literal: Is it not because years approach mulberry and elm dusk, calamity and worry are about to arrive—though one holds office at the royal court, one is permitted to resign affairs; how much more on a road of hardship and turmoil, when concern lies in what cannot be foreseen?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not because when years draw near sunset, trouble is at hand, one may hold office at court yet be allowed to withdraw—and how much more on a path of turmoil, when what lies ahead cannot be foreseen?

sentences.zh: 自非延年之辭允而義愜，夫豈或免。

translations.literal: Unless Yannian's words were fitting and his righteousness satisfying, how could he have escaped?
translations.idiomatic: Had Yannian's words not been apt and his conduct not justified, how could he have escaped?
